text: The Romans, who appear to have taken possession of this city under the Emperor Claudius, about 100 years after the invasion of Cassav gave to it the name of Argustus in ho-nour of this picture. Under the Roman government it was erected into a prohecture, and the inhabitants, though the name of citizens of Rome were conferred upon there, were not allowed to be governed by their own laws, but by military magistrates sent annually from Rome. It must then have accepted one degree of importance, because, in several of the _litterna_ of Antoninus, therod are described by him as beginning or ending at this period. The doubts interesting the author of the _itdorea_, and the time when they were drawn up, make this inference of less authority.
